context: A uni student interviews a retired engineer about industry history
purpose: Teach: 出現/就任/公社/策定/施工/従事/文部/室内

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただきありがとうございます。早速ですが、戦後の建設業界に出現した新しい技術について伺いたいです。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. To start, I'd like to ask about the new technologies that appeared in the postwar construction industry.
lines.style: Polite formal university student interviewing an elder respectfully

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、いいよ。私が現場に従事し始めた頃は、まだ日本道路公社が高速道路の整備計画を策定していた時代でね。
lines.en: Ah, sure. When I first started working on-site, it was still the era when the Japan Highway Public Corporation was drafting the expressway development plan.
lines.style: Warm reminiscent elder voice with nostalgic measured pacing

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。当時の施工管理は今とはかなり違ったのでしょうか。
lines.en: I see. Was construction management back then quite different from today?
lines.style: Curious attentive student probing for deeper historical context

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 全然違うよ。図面は手書きだし、室内で電卓を叩いて構造計算をしてた。文部省、今でいう文部科学省が出した基準書がバイブルでね。
lines.en: Completely different. Drawings were hand-drawn, and we did structural calculations indoors on calculators. The standards issued by the Ministry of Education, what's now MEXT, were our bible.
lines.style: Detailed explanatory tone with affectionate technical nostalgia

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 手書きですか。想像もつきません。当時の上司の方はどんな方でしたか。
lines.en: Hand-drawn? I can't even imagine. What was your supervisor like back then?
lines.style: Genuinely surprised young listener showing real interest

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 厳しい人だったよ。彼が部長に就任した日に、私たちを集めて『現場を一度も見ない設計者になるな』と言ってね。今でも覚えてる。
lines.en: He was a strict person. The day he was appointed division chief, he gathered us and said 'never become a designer who has never seen the site.' I still remember it.
lines.style: Reflective elder sharing a treasured formative memory

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 素敵な言葉ですね。最後に、これから業界に入る学生に何かメッセージはありますか。
lines.en: What a wonderful saying. Finally, do you have any message for students entering the industry now?
lines.style: Warm closing question with respectful interview conclusion tone

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 技術は変わっても、人と現場を大事にする心は変わらない。それだけは忘れないでほしいな。
lines.en: Even as technology changes, the spirit of valuing people and the worksite doesn't change. I just hope you don't forget that.
lines.style: Heartfelt parting wisdom from veteran to younger generation
